why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief. The builder brief has none of the verifier's fixtures: no clean1.jsonl, clean2.jsonl or bad.jsonl contents, and no `{bad}` or `{"torn":` rows. It also has none of its probe commands (`node B clean1.jsonl nope.jsonl bad.jsonl`, printf pipes, git diff merge-base, gh pr checks) and no PASS/FAIL wording. Its list of test cases and exit codes restates expect lines 3 and 5. The `-:` prefix comes from expect line 2. Both are allowed. The tip "Include a bad file next to the missing one to prove this" is a design hint for the builder's own tests and follows from "other files still checked and reported". It is not the verifier's exact inputs. "Do this check before reading anything" matches only the verifier's non-graded advisory. The only command the two briefs share is `npm test`, which is allowed.
